newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cash crudes lower, sour still under pressure.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cash crudes lower, sour still under pressure.

text.p: U.S. cash crude prices lost further ground Thursday, with West Texas Sour/Midland (WTS) and other sours leading the way down.

Benchmark West Texas Intermediate/Cushing (WTI) was down around five cents mid-morning compared with late Wednesday at around $19.35 as the sell-off started by bearish U.S. inventory reports on Tuesday and Wednesday continued.
WTS traded at $1.35 under WTI Thursday morning, matching Wednesday's lowest level and continuing the slump which has carried the differential down from around $1 under last week.
Eugene Island followed WTS lower and was indicated at $1.50 bid/$1.45 offered below WTI. It traded at $1.46 and $1.45 below.
"It (WTS) was very overheated anyway and it should be back out below $2 (discount)," said a trader for a medium-sized integrated oil company.
Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James (LLS) was showing signs of easing, traders said.
"There are a lot of people lining up to sell LLS at 24 and 25 (cents premium to WTI)," said a trader for an internationa major in Texas. A deal was done at 21 cents over.
LLS has improved its differential from a 25 cent discount over the last month, mainly due to the closed arbitrage and prospect of few North Sea Brent barrels in the weeks ahead.
Heavy Louisiana Sweet/Empire was quoted at 35/30 cents discount, though there wasn't much trading interest, traders said.

The August/September WTI contango widened out to around 15 cents early as the market weakened but came back in to 10 cents by noon. The Exchange for Physical premium was steady at about three cents value, brokers said.
